title: Both, Neither and Either: Choosing Between Two
summary: Use both, neither and either when precisely two people, objects or possibilities are involved. Distinguish two included, zero included and one possible choice; form expressions with of, coordinate ideas with and/nor/or, and contrast two-way choices with groups of three or more.
learningObjectives: Use both, neither and either accurately with two people, items or alternatives, including negative sentences.
Choose noun phrases with or without of and use of before us, you and them.
Connect parallel ideas using both ... and, neither ... nor and either ... or.
Choose either/neither/both for two options and any/none/all for larger groups.

explanation.heading: Three different ways to describe two
explanation.body: Use both when a statement is true of two people or things together: both proposals were accepted. Neither means not one and not the other: neither proposal was accepted. Either refers to one of the two, often when the choice does not matter: either proposal will work. With a singular countable noun use neither proposal or either proposal, but with both use a plural noun: both proposals.
explanation.example: Both microphones work, but neither speaker is connected.

explanation.heading: Either in an affirmative choice and a negative statement
explanation.body: In an affirmative sentence, either can mean whichever one of two options is chosen. In a negative sentence, not ... either usually means not the first and not the second: I did not choose either option. By contrast, I chose neither option states the same exclusion without an extra negative. Do not use a double negative such as I did not choose neither option in standard English.
explanation.example: I have not visited either gallery, so I cannot recommend one.

explanation.heading: With nouns, determiners and object pronouns
explanation.body: Use both, neither or either directly with a noun: both routes, neither route, either route. With a specific group introduced by the, these, my or a possessive, use both (of) my colleagues, neither of my colleagues or either of my colleagues. The of is optional after both before these determiners, but necessary after neither and either in these phrases. Before object pronouns, of is required: both of us, neither of them, either of you. Do not say both us or either them.
explanation.example: Neither of the two printers has the right cartridge, but both of them are switched on.

explanation.heading: Pair two ideas with and, nor or or
explanation.body: Use both ... and to include two parallel elements; neither ... nor to exclude both; and either ... or to present alternatives. Join like elements where possible: both careful and quick, neither emailed nor called, either on Tuesday or on Thursday. With neither ... nor and either ... or, verb agreement may depend on the nearest subject, so choose parallel singular subjects in controlled practice when clarity matters.
explanation.example: We can meet either before the workshop or after the final talk.

explanation.heading: Two options versus a larger set
explanation.body: Either, neither and both refer to exactly two. If three or more options are under discussion, use any for unrestricted choice, none for zero or all for the entire group. Neither of the two lockers was available is about two; none of the five lockers was available is about five. After neither of + a plural noun or pronoun, both singular and plural verb forms can occur; singular is useful in formal writing.
explanation.example: Of the four available designs, any one would fit our requirements.

left.label: Either: one is enough
left.example: Either entrance will take you to reception.
left.note: There are two entrances; either one can be chosen.

right.label: Both: the pair together
right.note: The statement describes the two entrances collectively.

left.label: Neither: positive verb
left.example: Neither of the two tablets works.
left.note: Neither already carries the negative meaning, so works is not additionally negated.

right.label: Not ... either: negative verb
right.example: I do not use either of the two tablets.
right.note: The negative verb plus either rejects both possibilities.

left.label: Exactly two: neither
left.example: Neither of the two lifts is running.
left.note: Neither is appropriate because the group contains two lifts.

right.label: More than two: none
right.example: None of the six lifts is running.
right.note: None, not neither, refers to a group of six.

examples.sentence: Both instructors have experience teaching adult learners.
examples.note: Both modifies a plural noun and includes the two instructors.

examples.sentence: Neither exit leads directly to the car park.
examples.note: Neither is followed by a singular noun because exactly two exits are considered.

examples.sentence: You can use either of these two meeting rooms.
examples.note: Either of + these two specifies that one of the rooms can be chosen.

examples.sentence: Both of us received the revised timetable.
examples.note: Of is required before the object pronoun us.

examples.sentence: The parcel was neither damaged nor delayed.
examples.note: Neither ... nor joins two negative descriptions of the same parcel.

examples.sentence: I did not recognise either of the two voices on the recording.
examples.note: Not ... either excludes both voices without a double negative.

commonMistakes.why: When both directly modifies the plural noun lamps, do not put the before both.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Either of them are fine; I only need one key.
commonMistakes.correct: Either of them is fine; I only need one key.
commonMistakes.why: Either of refers to one of two options and commonly takes a singular verb in careful writing.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Both us know how to use the scanner.
commonMistakes.correct: Both of us know how to use the scanner.
commonMistakes.why: Before an object pronoun such as us, both must be followed by of.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We have two offers, but neither offer the hours I need.
commonMistakes.correct: We have two offers, but neither offers the hours I need.
commonMistakes.why: When neither directly modifies no noun and stands for not one of two, it takes a singular verb in this construction.

studyTips: Sketch two circles: shade both for both, neither for neither, and just one possible circle for either. Then verbalise each meaning.
Practise the same two-person sentence as both colleagues, both of my colleagues and both of them; notice when of is required.
For every sentence with neither ... nor or either ... or, check that the two joined elements have matching grammatical roles.

exercises.prompt: There are exactly two service desks, and both are closed. ___ desk can help us right now.
exercises.feedback: Neither desk means that the two service desks are unavailable.

exercises.prompt: Two seats are free on this train. You may take ___ seat; it makes no difference to me.
exercises.feedback: Either seat indicates a free choice between the two seats.

exercises.prompt: Exactly two students entered the final round, and ___ students received a certificate.
exercises.feedback: Both modifies the plural noun students directly and includes the two finalists.

exercises.prompt: We have tried exactly two passwords, but ___ worked.
exercises.feedback: Neither of them means that the first password and the second password both failed.

exercises.prompt: The twins were delighted with their results. ___ of them passed the exam. (word meaning the two together)
exercises.feedback: Both of them contains of before the object pronoun them, and includes both twins.

exercises.prompt: The two conference rooms are the same size. You can book ___ room. (one word meaning whichever of the two you choose)
exercises.feedback: Either with a singular noun means that one of two is an acceptable choice.

exercises.prompt: I checked the two documents, but ___ of them included the signature. (word meaning not one and not the other)
exercises.feedback: Neither of them describes two missing signatures and uses of before them.

exercises.prompt: The presentation was ___ informative and entertaining. (word that pairs with and)
exercises.feedback: Both ... and joins two descriptions that are true together.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The both windows were left open overnight.
acceptedAnswers: Both windows were left open overnight.
exercises.feedback: Both goes straight before the plural noun windows; the is not used in this pattern.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The manager spoke to both them before making a decision.
acceptedAnswers: The manager spoke to both of them before making a decision.
exercises.feedback: Both requires of before the object pronoun them.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: There are only two printers, but neither them can print in colour.
acceptedAnswers: There are only two printers, but neither of them can print in colour.
exercises.feedback: Neither requires of before the object pronoun them.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We can schedule the inspection either on Monday nor on Wednesday.
acceptedAnswers: We can schedule the inspection either on Monday or on Wednesday.
exercises.feedback: The parallel conjunction with either is or, not nor.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use the exact facts: two cameras; work properly. Start with “Both cameras” and say one complete sentence.
speakingExercises.feedback: Both + plural noun includes the two cameras; the plural verb is work.

speakingExercises.prompt: Ask one yes/no question starting with “Can” using these exact facts: either of you; operate; the projector. Address exactly two people.
acceptedAnswers: Can either of you operate the projector?
speakingExercises.feedback: Either of you refers to one of the two people; of before you is necessary.

speakingExercises.prompt: Turn this fact into one negative sentence using “neither”: of two assistants, not one is available. Begin with “Neither assistant”.
speakingExercises.feedback: Neither assistant expresses that both assistants are unavailable without another negative.

speakingExercises.prompt: A visitor may enter through the north gate or the south gate, with no preference. Say one sentence starting “You can use”, and end with “gate”. Include the word “either”.
speakingExercises.feedback: Either gate allows the visitor to choose one of the two gates.

speakingExercises.prompt: Transform this sentence using neither ... nor, changing neither action: “Mara did not call and did not send a message.” Begin with “Mara”.
acceptedAnswers: Mara neither called nor sent a message.
speakingExercises.feedback: Neither ... nor joins two actions that Mara did not perform.

speakingExercises.prompt: Two meeting dates are possible: Tuesday and Thursday. Say one sentence beginning with “We can meet”, using “either on” before Tuesday and “or on” before Thursday.
acceptedAnswers: We can meet either on Tuesday or on Thursday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Either ... or joins parallel prepositional phrases for the two possible dates.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say exactly two short sentences from these facts: there are two laptops; neither laptop is charged; both laptops belong to us. Start your sentences with “Neither laptop” and “Both laptops”.
acceptedAnswers: Neither laptop is charged. Both laptops belong to us.
speakingExercises.feedback: Neither rejects the charge state of two laptops, while both includes their shared ownership.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct only the missing preposition and say the complete sentence: “Both us attended the safety briefing.”
acceptedAnswers: Both of us attended the safety briefing.
speakingExercises.feedback: The object pronoun us requires of after both.

listeningExercises.audioText: The two elevators are out of service, so neither will take us to the fifth floor.
listeningExercises.prompt: How many of the elevators can take the group upstairs?
listeningExercises.feedback: Neither indicates that both of the two elevators are unavailable.

listeningExercises.audioText: I can collect the documents on Tuesday or Thursday. Either day is fine with me.
listeningExercises.prompt: What scheduling preference does the speaker express?
choices: One of the two days is acceptable.
listeningExercises.feedback: Either day means the speaker accepts whichever of the two dates is chosen.

listeningExercises.audioText: Both of us reviewed the proposal before the meeting began.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word expression immediately before “reviewed”.
listeningExercises.feedback: The audio says both of us, including both people; of is required before us.

listeningExercises.audioText: The designer offered two layouts, but I did not approve either of them.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did the speaker decide about the layouts?
choices: Only the second layout was approved.
listeningExercises.feedback: Did not approve either means neither of the two layouts was accepted.

listeningExercises.audioText: The workshop was both informative and practical, so we will use its advice next week.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which two qualities does the speaker attribute to the workshop?
choices: It provided useful information and practical guidance.
listeningExercises.feedback: Both ... and combines two positive qualities: informative and practical.

listeningExercises.audioText: We contacted five suppliers, but none of them could deliver the material in time.
listeningExercises.prompt: How many of the contacted suppliers could deliver on time?
listeningExercises.feedback: None of them means that zero of the five contacted suppliers could deliver on time.

listeningExercises.audioText: Neither of the two spare batteries is fully charged.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two words immediately before “the two spare batteries”.
listeningExercises.feedback: Neither of introduces the two specified batteries, and means zero of the pair.

listeningExercises.audioText: The headphones were neither cheap nor comfortable, so I returned them.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word connector heard between “were” and “comfortable”, including the adjective in between.
listeningExercises.feedback: The words neither cheap nor coordinate two negative descriptions of the headphones.
